name: Lyral
reason: EU Cosmetics Regulation Annex II prohibits HICC (Reg. (EU) 2022/1181), so 0 is the right cap -- but it is NOT an IFRA figure. The IFRA 51st restricts HICC at 0.2% (IFRA_STD_044), and the old seed CSV recorded the ban as 'IFRA 49th: prohibited', which is the wrong instrument. The row lives here so the provenance says which regulator actually forbids it.

name: Guaiacol
reason: house cap, not an IFRA figure: no IFRA standard lists guaiacol. The perfumer's own ceiling on a phenolic smoke material that dominates in overdose.

name: 2-Isopropyl Phenol
reason: house cap, not an IFRA figure: phenolic creosote, dominates in overdose, and no IFRA standard lists it.

name: Anethole ex Star Anise
reason: house cap on ESTRAGOLE CONTENT, not on anethole: star anise oil carries estragole (IFRA_STD_099, cat-4 0.014%) and anethole itself is not restricted. The figure keeps the oil's estragole below the estragole limit.

name: Metal Oxazole
reason: house cap, NOT an IFRA figure: no IFRA standard lists this substance and cat-4 permits 100%; 2% is the perfumer's own ceiling on the finished product.

name: Calone 1951
reason: IFRA 52nd amendment draft: 0.47% of the finished product, cat-4. The 51st amendment (the workbook this pipeline imports) has no Calone standard, so the figure enters as a house cap until the 52nd is published and imported. Supplied by the perfumer, 2026-11-06.
